verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The product is the same: `labelMask n k (q, X) = dyadicMask n q * slowMask n k X` is η_γ(R,Z,T) = χ_ℓ(q)χ_{ℓ,a}(R,Z,T), with `dyadicMask` the band cutoff (its tsupport is exactly q/Q ∈ [1/2,2]) and `slowMask` the grid cutoff; `PhysicalWaveSum.physicalMask` (and the curried `PartitionedCovariance.physicalMask`) is the composite η_γ ∘ C_ℓ, since `physicalSlowMask D n k x = slowMask n k (slowCoordinates D n x)`. Encoding differences: (i) Lean carries q as an independent first coordinate of the point (ℝ × Position) rather than as the function q(r,z,t), and the Position coordinate is (r, z, τ), so K_γ = `tsupport (PhysicalWaveSum.physicalMask D L)` is the closed support in (q, r, z, τ) rather than in (r,z,t); (ii) Lean's labels carry a sign in `SlotColoring.Label = ℕ × (Grid × Bool)` but `physicalMask` reads only `L.1` and `L.2.1`, which is exactly the paper's η_{(ℓ,a,+)} = η_{(ℓ,a,-)} stated just after (6.9); (iii) the named set `labelRegion` is the product of the two closed supports, a closed superset of K_γ rather than K_γ itself — `physicalMask_tsupport_subset` proves the inclusion, and the downstream disjointness arguments use `labelRegion` in place of K_γ.
